oil.summary: Crude ended the week nursing steep losses despite a marginal daily dip: WTI settled around $77.28 (-0.03% on the day, -8.74% on the week) and Brent at $82.32 (-0.22% d/d, -8.67% w/w). The dominant driver was the US-Iran agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which unwound the geopolitical risk premium that had built up after three tankers were damaged in the Gulf earlier this week. RBOB gasoline was the session's standout mover, collapsing 7.69% on the day and nearly 16% on the week, amplifying the bearish signal. Bullish offsets were limited but present: Ukraine struck one of Russia's largest oil refineries in a long-range drone campaign, China's July crude imports rebounded 22% month-on-month to 8.45 mb/d, and a Saudi-Pakistan-Turkey defense pact added background geopolitical noise. CME options markets price a 77% probability of an OPEC production increase at the next meeting.
drivers: US-Iran Strait of Hormuz agreement triggered sharp sell-off, erasing the conflict risk premium built over the prior week
China crude imports rebounded 22% m/m in July to 8.45 mb/d, providing a partial demand-side cushion
Ukrainian long-range drone strikes on Russian refineries and shadow fleet vessels introduced supply-disruption risk but failed to arrest the broader bearish trend

gas.summary: Henry Hub nudged higher by 1.63% on the day to $2.683/MMBtu, but remains down 2.33% on the week and over 10% on the month, reflecting soft fundamentals. TTF fell 1.45% to €54.96/MWh, extending a near-7% weekly decline even as the monthly trend remains up roughly 10%. Vessel traffic through the Strait of Hormuz dropped sharply during the week amid US-Iran uncertainty, a development that carries LNG transit implications, though the subsequent reopening agreement should ease those concerns. Structurally, Southeast Asia's gas-fired power buildout is reportedly stalling due to gas shortages and high prices, pointing to persistent regional demand-supply mismatches. The headline flow for this sector is thinner than oil today; no major storage or production data crossed the wire.
drivers: Strait of Hormuz shipping disruption during the week weighed on LNG transit sentiment, with the reopening agreement now providing partial relief
Southeast Asia gas shortages and high prices are undermining planned gas-fired power capacity additions, signaling structural regional tightness
Henry Hub remains under sustained monthly pressure (-10.92%), suggesting weak near-term US domestic demand or ample supply despite today's modest bounce

power.summary: EU Carbon (EUA) bucked the energy complex's broader weakness, gaining 1.02% on the day to $78.43/EUA and posting a solid +1.84% on the week and nearly +5% on the month. The constructive carbon tone aligns with a headline out of Europe reporting power prices spiking to €500/MWh as intense summer drought and heatwaves suppress hydropower output and drive air-conditioning load. A drone attack on a UAE nuclear power plant added to supply-security concerns earlier this week, though details remain limited in the feed. Southeast Asia's faltering gas-fired power buildout, driven by fuel shortages and elevated prices, underscores a wider global theme of electricity system stress. Ukraine's depleted air-defense capacity and ongoing Russian missile campaigns remain a background risk to European grid infrastructure.
drivers: European electricity prices spiked to €500/MWh as drought curtails hydro generation and summer heat drives record air-conditioning demand, supporting carbon prices
Drone attack on a UAE nuclear power plant earlier this week highlighted acute energy-infrastructure vulnerability in the Gulf
Southeast Asia's gas-fired power buildout stalling due to fuel shortages points to broader structural pressure on power system adequacy across emerging markets
